archetypes.name: architecture
archetypes.rationale: Plan describes a monolithic design-step0.sh with --phase flags, but the new harness explicitly checks design-step0-degraded.sh, design-step0-route.sh, and design-step0-init.sh as separate wrappers — a structural divergence that may leave phase contracts undefined or untested.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan specifies a single design-step0.sh with --phase initial|resume-issue|resume-degraded, but the new assert_degraded_tools_gate_fence in scripts/test-design-structure.sh checks for design-step0-degraded.sh, design-step0-route.sh, and design-step0-init.sh as distinct scripts (diff lines 762–778). Verify whether those sub-scripts exist and whether their phase contracts — missing-env tolerance for initial, skip-setup and no-new-DESIGN_TMPDIR for resume phases — are separately exercised by the harness or fall between the two decomposition levels. Examine the inter-wrapper state sidecar .design-step0-route-state.env that design-step0-route.sh writes and design-step0-init.sh reads (diff lines 776–777): check whether missing-file and partial-write conditions are defended, and whether all route KVs consumed by SKILL.md are still reachable after the split. Confirm that the SKILL.md stdout allowlist (STEP0_STATUS, ROUTE, and every route/clarify/cancel key) is emitted as a single coherent block under the new decomposed layout. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: risk-integration
archetypes.rationale: test-design-structure.sh shrank from ~2050 to ~500 lines, removing dozens of behavioral contract assertions; the new Python fence-checker enforces --claude-pid on ALL fences, not just Step 0 and Step 5c, producing false CI failures for every intermediate wrapper.
archetypes.prompt_body: scripts/test-design-structure.sh was reduced from ~2050 lines to ~500 lines (diff lines 122–128); dozens of named contract assertions were removed — including assert_thin_fence region pins, assert_step_completion_sentinels, assert_folded_sentinel_writes, assert_backward_reentry_guards, and assert_deleted_prelude_guards. Identify which of these contracts are now covered by wrapper-specific tests versus entirely unguarded, paying particular attention to sentinel ordering invariants (pause-before-work, guard-scoped writes) and the SIMPLE-branch no-standalone-fence rule. Also inspect the new assert_design_skill_bash_fences_are_wrappers Python block (diff lines 386–434): the unconditional --claude-pid check at lines 411–414 applies to every fence, but the plan requires --claude-pid only on Step 0 and Step 5c wrappers (plan.txt lines 619–620), so any intermediate-step fence that omits it will fail CI. Finally, confirm that the new .pause-save-complete sentinel written by design-pause-save.sh (diff lines 28–29) is actually consumed by design-step3-entry.sh as the harness asserts (diff line 782) and not silently ignored on failure paths. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
